subject: Post-demo: CMK/KMS & HSM integration checklist + next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Brooks <daniel.brooks@fintechco.com>, Rachel Stein <rachel.stein@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: CMK/KMS & HSM integration checklist + next steps

Hi Daniel / Rachel — thanks again for the call this afternoon. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap of requirements we heard
- Data residency: primary tenant + S3 logs must remain in eu-west-1 for production.
- PII controls: no plaintext customer PII persisted beyond session; token redaction for logs.
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit + AES-256 at-rest. Customer-managed key (CMEK) required for sensitive buckets; preference for AWS KMS or external HSM (FIPS 140-2/3).
- Audit/logging: immutable access logs, retention configurable up to 7 years; need attestable key-rotation history.

Attachments: redwood-cmk-integration-guide.pdf (integration steps), SOC2-summary-2025.pdf (controls summary).

Proposed next steps
1) Vivek to share technical checklist for integrating FinTechCo KMS with Redwood Private (API endpoints, auth flows, supported key types). Target: 24 Feb.
2) FinTechCo to confirm procurement contact and timeline for SOW + PoC (we suggested a 4-week pilot).
3) Karthik to loop in security for a short checklist review (key rotation, signing, audit proofs).
4) Lauren to draft commercial/term options (CMEK add-on, Dedicated vs Private).

Can you confirm procurement contact and whether you prefer native AWS KMS or an external HSM-backed key store? Also flag any constraints around HSM vendor (Thales, Gemalto, AWS CloudHSM) or PKCS#11 compatibility.

Thanks — happy to schedule a 30-min technical workshop next week if helpful.

Best,

Jasmine Liu
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0132
From: Daniel Brooks <daniel.brooks@fintechco.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Stein <rachel.stein@fintechco.com>
Cc: procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: CMK/KMS & HSM integration checklist + next steps

Jasmine — thanks for the detailed recap, very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Preference: we prefer AWS KMS for initial rollout, but must support an external HSM-backed key for escrowed keys later (CloudHSM or on-prem Thales). The gating factor is that keys originating in our HSM must never be exportable.
- Logging: we need proof that no plaintext tokens or PII are stored in your debug logs or any intermediate caches. If you can provide a short statement or config toggle that redacts token-level data in logs, that would help procurement.
- Retention: 7 years for audit logs is non-negotiable for our compliance team.

Procurement contact: procurement@fintechco.com (CC’d). We’ll aim to get SOW comments back within 5 business days once we have the integration approach documented.

Can Vivek share the exact KMS API calls and the flow for a rotate-or-revoke event? We need to understand how Redwood surfaces key provenance in the audit trail.

Thanks,
Daniel
Head of Platform Security | FinTechCo
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Brooks <daniel.brooks@fintechco.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: CMK/KMS & HSM integration checklist + next steps

Daniel — quick technical answers inline and a short integration checklist.

Summary answers
- Supported keybackends: AWS KMS (symmetric & asymmetric), AWS CloudHSM (via KMS or direct PKCS#11 integration), and external HSMs via PKCS#11 for Redwood Private. Keys marked as non-exportable are enforced by the HSM/KMS.
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 mandatory for all customer traffic; mutual TLS option for Private control plane.
- At-rest: AES-256 with envelope encryption using customer CMKs when enabled.
- Logs: token redaction is available as a configuration flag for request/response payloads; we also support prefix-only KV caching to avoid storing full user inputs.

Integration checklist (target deliverables by 2026-02-24)
1) Auth: provide AWS KMS Key ARN or PKCS#11 credentials for HSM. For PKCS#11 we need vendor, slot, and path to library.
2) Network: provide network diagram and peering expectations (attached template).
3) Audit: indicate required retention window (you flagged 7y — we will surface that to ops). We will include a signed audit proof for key rotations.
4) PoC: we’ll spin up a Private tenant in eu-west-1, mount your CMK, and run a short write/read workload over 2 weeks.
5) SOW items: service levels for key availability and rotation SLA (proposed 99.95% for CMEK operations).

I’ll attach a short snippet of the API call flows in the technical workshop; for now: 
- KMS Encrypt: Redwood calls encrypt with your KMS using a transient data key, we never persist plaintext.
- Rotate: on rotate, Redwood keyswitches to the new envelope key and emits rotation event to your audit trail containing old/new key ARNs (no key material).

Attachments referenced: network-diagram-template.vsdx (attached), redwood-cmk-integration-guide.pdf (previous).

If you’re good with the checklist, we can schedule the technical workshop (30–45 min) on Wed/Thu this week.

— Vivek
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com

Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: CMK/KMS & HSM integration checklist + next steps

Thanks — a couple of procurement/security asks to add to the SOW: 
- We need a short attestation that Redwood will not persist plaintext PII beyond the session and that redaction is enabled for the pilot.
- Please confirm retention controls will allow us to set different retention windows per log type (access logs vs debug traces).
- For the PoC, we’ll provide an account that only exposes the KMS ARN; Redwood must not be able to export the key.

Also, can you include an initial estimate for billing impact when CMEK is enabled vs Redwood-managed keys? Procurement will need that for budget.

Rachel
